title: Telling stories about the past
title_target: រឿងកាលពីមុន — ruèng kaal pii mun
goal: Tell a story longer than one sentence — with linking words, time order, and ធ្លាប់ for things you've experienced.
bekal: use ធ្លាប់ for "have ever" and tell it apart from បាន
link sentences with បន្ទាប់មក, ប៉ុន្តែ, ព្រោះ, ដូច្នេះ
tell a story in time order
ask about other people's experiences with ធ្លាប់ … ទេ?

dialogs.title: កិច្ចសន្ទនា — Travel stories on the porch
dialogs.intro: Ani is back from Battambang and tells Sreymom all about it. Notice that **not one verb changes form** in the whole story — time is built by time words and linking words.

grammars.title: ⚠️ ធ្លាប់ (have ever) versus បាន (got to)
body: Both go before the verb and both have to do with the past, but they do different jobs. **ធ្លាប់ expresses experience** — that you've done something at some point, whenever. **បាន expresses that an event actually took place**, usually at a particular time.

Say it
Translation
Feel
rows: ខ្ញុំធ្លាប់ទៅអង្គរ
ម្សិលមិញខ្ញុំទៅអង្គរ
ខ្ញុំបានទៅអង្គរមែន
I did go to Angkor, really
ខ្ញុំមិនដែលទៅទេ

after: ⚠️ The negative of ធ្លាប់ is **not** មិនធ្លាប់ but **មិនដែល … ទេ** (*min-dael … té*). This pair is irregular and has to be memorized whole: ធ្លាប់ for "have ever", មិនដែល…ទេ for "have never".
Answering a ធ្លាប់ … ទេ? question follows the pattern from Unit 4: **repeat the verb**. The "yes" answer is ធ្លាប់, the "no" answer is មិនដែលទេ.

grammars.title: Linking words that build a story
body: Telling a story means stringing sentences together. These linking words are enough for every story at A1, and they all go at the **start** of the second sentence.
after: ⚠️ **ហើយ has two jobs**, and you already know one from Unit 11. At the end of a sentence it means "already"; at the start it means "and, then". Its position decides.

**ព្រោះ (because) always comes before the cause**, just like English: ខ្ញុំដេក ព្រោះអស់កម្លាំង ("I slept because I was exhausted"). And **ដូច្នេះ comes before the result**: ខ្ញុំអស់កម្លាំង ដូច្នេះខ្ញុំដេក.

grammars.title: Putting events in order
body: Since the verbs don't change, the order of events has to be spelled out. Here are the sequence markers used most in stories.
after: ⚠️ **កាលពី** (*kaal-pii*) contains the Sanskrit word **កាល** (*kāla*, "time"). កាលពីមុន means "in the past", កាលពីតូច means "when I was little". Once you recognize it, a whole family of Khmer time words opens up.

blocks.text: Here's a story frame you can fill with your own experience. Write your version on paper, then say it out loud. This is the most useful practice in the whole book — and the only one that really trains you to speak more than one sentence.

blocks.title: Three places every Cambodian will ask you about
items: **អង្គរវត្ត (Angkor Wat).** If you haven't been, everyone will tell you to go. If you have, they'll ask ស្អាតទេ? and wait for your answer with a smile.
**បាត់ដំបង, កំពត, កែប (Battambang, Kampot, Kep).** Three small towns Cambodians are proud of and that tour groups rarely visit.

**Their own ស្រុកកំណើត (home province).** If your neighbor mentions their province, ask ស្អាតទេ? and ធ្លាប់ … ទេ? — the conversation will go on much longer than you expect, and that's exactly what makes your Khmer grow.

Have you ever been to Battambang?
I have! I just got back yesterday.
The first day I slept all afternoon.
After that my friend took me to see the cave.
It was fun, but a little scary.
I never have.
